title: Reading Drill — Evaluating discounts at a cinema — Preparing a second trial
description: One short passage, six questions. Recommended time: 10 minutes.

passages.title: Evaluating discounts at a cinema — Preparing a second trial
passages.body:
**A** In Elmbrook, work on popular screenings still having empty seats after booking had already produced a small collection of ticket scans. The cinema manager used this material to plan a second trial. The first report contained several different figures, but for the second trial the group agreed to publish one main outcome: the share of reservations used.

**B** The group kept same-day reminders for the new trial, which was planned to run for ten weeks. Volunteers were shown a sample record before starting. They were also asked to describe anything unusual in a separate note, so later readers could tell the difference between an ordinary value and one taken during a disruption.

**C** The trial design stated that last-minute film changes should be recorded even when everything else appeared normal. If this information was missing, the team would leave the field blank rather than infer an answer. It would publish a provisional finding and label it clearly if too few readings were available for a reliable result.
